ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a plus-shaped arrangement made of five blank squares. There is one center square, one square immediately to the left and one immediately to the right forming a horizontal row of three squares, and one square immediately above and one immediately below forming a vertical column of three squares. Reasoning: Let the number in the center square be c, and let the common horizontal and vertical sum be S. The five numbers are 1, 4, 7, 10, and 13, with total 1 + 4 + 7 + 10 + 13 = 35. If we add the horizontal row sum and the vertical column sum, every square is counted once except the center square, which is counted twice. Therefore 2S = 35 + c. To maximize S, we maximize c. The largest possible center value is 13, giving 2S = 35 + 13 = 48, so S = 24. This is feasible because the remaining numbers 1, 4, 7, and 10 can be split into two pairs with equal sum 11: 1 + 10 = 11 and 4 + 7 = 11. Put one pair in the left and right squares and the other pair in the top and bottom squares. Then each row or column has sum 13 + 11 = 24.

In the image structure, adding the horizontal row sum and vertical column sum counts every square once, except the center square is counted twice. Therefore 2S = 35 + c. To maximize S, maximize c subject to feasibility. Since c can be at most 13, try c = 13: then S = (35 + 13)/2 = 24. Check feasibility by splitting the remaining numbers 1, 4, 7, 10 into two pairs with equal sum 11: 1 + 10 and 4 + 7. Put one pair in the left/right positions and the other in the top/bottom positions. Thus the largest possible sum is 24.
